text:
four books on my shelf asking to be re-read

1. Siddartha…this is probably the most well known and most well-read/consensus pick. 

I read it 4-5 years ago and just remember closing the final page and immediately saying “that was one of the best fucking books I’ve ever read.” 

no lag time, nothing, just…"where in the top 10 is this going."

one really funny thing with novels/fiction, which is entirely normal, is to remember very little of what u read...ask LLMs, they'll confirm. you're not crazy.

its the mood, the vibe, the aura of a text that really stays with you.

2. Jung...this is a short book (100 pages?) but I remember getting a ton out of it. type of stuff that shifts ur worldview and outlook on human nature/society

for Jung, I'd vote that its as good a place to start as any, and if u like it then go deeper.

3. In Praise of Folly

Also not a long book, very old one (written in ~1500), can be dense at times...I didn't like it until halfway through then realized "oh shit, this is amazing and I am going to have to re-read it."

books this old only survive for 1 reason...they are jammed full of truths about human nature, usually the unpleasant ones (see Machiavelli, La Rochefoucauld, Pascal)

very similar book (novella?) to Samuel Johnson's Rasselas. you quickly recognize u are in the presence of a superior mind and gifted observer of human nature, who is holding a flamethrower and systematically melting down the world as you knew it...they leave no stone unturned. both are masterworks in that regard

4. last...Lost Illusions

I read "Pere Goriot" before this and thought it was okay

Lost Illusions, kind of similar to Monte Cristo in that there is a brief setup period (50-100 pages?) and then the rest is straight payoff.

the plot here, a young man goes off into society and sees it for the disgusting beast that it truly is -- chesterfield's "coarse pulleys and dirty ropes" -- and Balzac is wicked with the pen.

after finishing it, went right to the #2 spot in my "favorite novels of all time" only behind War and Peace

--

if I had to pick one, do Siddartha...for whatever reason the "afterglow" of that one is strongest in my mind.
